HMS Caroline, Belfast

LocationAlexandra Dock, Queens Rd, Belfast BT3 9DT, United Kingdom
Visited4 January 2017
WebsiteHMS Caroline | National Museum of the Royal Navy

Museum Report

HMS Caroline is a British light cruiser from World War 1 - and the last surviving vessel from the Battle of Jutland. She survived by virtue of the fact that for many years she was the Headquarters Ship for the Ulster Division, Royal Navy Reserve (RNR). When that service finally came to an end, she was taken over by the National Museum of the Royal Navy and opened as a museum ship in Alexandra Dock - very close to the slipway where Titanic was built, which you can still walk around.

Unfortunately, as I discovered, they close Caroline during the winter time, so when I visited Belfast I was limited to skulking around the perimeter trying to take photos through, or over the fence.

Her profile has been compromised somewhat in her current configuration due to the deckhouses that were erected on her while she was the RNR Drill Ship - however we should be grateful that she survived - a rare example of a World War 1 warship still afloat.
